svg.title: The counter block keeps two-digit counts apart at any digit width
svg.desc: Two arms of one rendered transition row, shown from column 100 to column 149, columns counted from zero. At the base revision the block's three separator columns have been reclaimed for the reason, so a single-digit count's own pad is the only gap a cell has: counts (10,12,0,0) print as 10w12b 0u 0q and (99,99,0,0) as 99w99b, and no column separates a two-digit count from the bucket beside it. At the head revision each cell is its digits followed by its bucket letter with no padding, one space separates every pair of cells, and the block reserves the four widest cells plus its three separators, so the same counts print 10w 12b 0u 0q. A single-digit fleet leaves the spare columns as trailing space at the block's right edge, so the block keeps its width and the clause after it begins at one column whatever the counts: 123 at head, where it began at 120. The block is fifteen columns wide at head against twelve at base, the three columns the reason clause gives up.
svg.text: The counter block: a two-digit count is its own token, and the block keeps its width
One rendered transition row per arm, columns 100–149, counted from zero.
base 452b043e — the block's separator columns were reclaimed for the reason, so a pad is a cell's only gap
No column separates a two-digit count from the bucket beside it.
the abutting pair — one token, unreadable as two
a single-digit fleet had a gap by luck: its own pad
the clause began at column 120 — three columns earlier
1f102e24 — one space between every pair of cells; the block reserves its widest width
the clause begins here, whatever the counts
The block is fifteen columns wide whatever the counts (twelve at base), so the clause after it begins at one column rather than following a wider fleet.
